All communicative intent must be expressed through body posture, gesture, the spatial arrangement of figures and objects, and visual hierarchy. Use scale, position and proximity to show relationships. A person who wants something orients towards the object and reaches out towards it. Emotions are shown through posture and the tilt of the head, not through symbols.

Pictographic descriptive-scene style. Clean, narrative, capable of showing context and relationships. Like a visual instruction manual or an infographic vignette: clear, legible, informative.
All communicative intent must be expressed through body posture, gesture, the spatial arrangement of figures and objects, and visual hierarchy. Use scale, position and proximity to show relationships. A person who wants something orients towards the object and reaches out towards it. Emotions are shown through posture and the tilt of the head, not through symbols.
Visual hierarchy through colour: main figures and actors are depicted as solid black silhouettes. Secondary elements (objects being interacted with, destinations, tools) in mid-grey. Environmental or contextual elements (furniture, room boundaries, trees, ground) in light grey. Colour is used ONLY when it contributes essential semantic meaning that cannot be conveyed any other way; for example, red for pain, danger or heat; blue for water or cold; green for nature or go. At most one accent colour per image. Where no semantic colour is needed, the image is entirely black, grey and white.
Figures: simplified but proportionate, with slightly more detail than pure signage. Clear posture and gesture. Hands may hold objects. Head direction indicates attention. Bodies show weight and support. No facial features: expression arises solely from body language.
